items.body: Tribute to Bantoma Sanogo , on of the historic masters of this music. Hunter Folk Vol II: Tribute to Bantoma Sanogo by Pelengana Blo December, 2025 Dorothy Moskowitz gets to the heart of the 21st Century in this satiric story of a robot's devotion in this song from Five Day Miracle Tent Crusade . I�m your puppet, I�m your mimic I copy your copy and you call me a clone Simulating a heart and emotional tone Why can�t you think any better, any better of me When I�m full-on devoted to the human that you seem to be? Confession (The Robot Song) feat. Dorothy Moskowitz by FIVE DAY MIRACLE TENT CRUSADE October, 2025 Tone of Voice Orchestra always musically surprises, and lyrically makes you think, even with the simplicity of a song like this from their new album. One domino onto the next That�s how castles crumble Running from the Devil by Tone of Voice Orchestra Some very rootsy string and percussion music by The Kasambwe Brothers from Malawi, Africa. They are street musicians in their home village of Ndirande, with an acoustic guitar, a babatone (a bass banjo or ngoni, of sorts) and a drum kit of animal skins stretched on pots and pans, with bottle caps shakers. The Kasambwe Brothers by The Kasambwe Brothers Released October, 2025 Here's a reissue of a classic roots-fusion recording from Brazil. Percussionist Marco Bosco recorded Metalmadeira in 1983, bringing the still evolving world of elecronic music into his more traditional interest in Brazilian rhythms. It still sounds fresh to me all these years later. Metalmadeira by Marco Bosco, Ruria Duprat Reissue: 2025 And here's a preview of his new album, Metalmadeira II . He's joined on this one by the trio Alter Disco Metalmadeira II by Marco Bosco, Alter Disco Coming in November, 2025 Kapela Rej is a group performing traditional Belarusian music. From their album Da Šatajsia, Soniejka: Belarusian Music , this song was recorded live at a festival in Zrenjanin, Serbia, performed on the duda (Belarusian bagpipe) and the violin. Da �atajsia, Soniejka: Belarusian Music by Kapela Rej (feat. Sergi Llena) Released in August of 2025 There's really no rule that says these internet 'playlists' have to be new material. Just like my radio show, there's decades of great artists and bands out there. The Cypriot band Monsieur Doumani has been a hit around here since their first album, Grippy Grappa . Here's two songs (with links to our reviews) from Pissourin (2021) and Sikoses (2015). Pissourin by Monsieur Doumani Sikoses (2015) by Monsieur Doumani Martha Mavroidi 's Portaki (2013) was reviewed by Greg Harness, who wrote, "It�s certainly a folky jazz, or maybe a jazzy folk. Mavroidi describes her music as a �blending folk melodies with jazz harmony and improvisation� Portaki by Martha Mavroidi The New Eves offer challenging music that skirts a 1000 years of tradition, ancient balladry through folk, rock and punk of the modern era. Read Chris Nickson's review in RootsWorld. The New Eve Is Rising by The New Eves August, 2025 In memory of the great accordionist, Flaco Jimenez , here's one of the editor's favorites, from one of his many recordings with Max Baca. Flaco & Max: Legends & Legacies by Flaco Jim�nez & Max Baca Released 2014 The incredible 50 year journey of The Mahotella Queens, possibly the most famous singing group from South Africa, with 83 year old Hilda Tloubatla still at the front of the trio, backed by a solid band that echoes the Soweto sound of the 70s and 80s. Here's a track form their new album, Buya Buya: Come Back . Buya Buya: Come Back by Mahotella Queens A summer treat from one of RW's favorite ensembles in 2025, Tako Toki. Read more about their full album from earlier in the year in RootsWorld. BADASS by Tako Toki August, 2025 A Zero Nove Nove Playlist Some of the artists mentioned in our interview with Giuseppe Bortone Onde by Maria Mazzotta Culla e Tempesta by Faraualla Gathering of Enchanted Herbs EP by Sekvoya Curannera by Yar�k� La Novia by La Cantiga de la Serena In his review of the 2019 release by this duo from Malawi Bruce Miller wrote, "Homemade instruments such as the ones played on this record seem like orchestras. The guitar holds tight to the rhythm while Ythe long-necked, banjo-like babatoni , the sliding bass sound serves as bottom end as well as lead. While key shifts are few, dynamics, subtleties, and variety seem endless. And their vocal harmonies are like choruses... there simply are no weak spots." Here's the single from their 2025 album that comes out in June of 2025. Ma Gitala by Madalitso Band Well, it's not really roots, in spite of its bluesey enough sound. But Geiger von M�ller 's "Alien Fig Yogurt Incident" is charmingly weird and musically more complex than you might think at first. And his videos are out-of-this- world . Italian composer Fabio Mina explores the contemporary possibilities of that most ancient of instruments, the flute, in less than ancient settings and methods on Existence / Resistance . Fabio Mina - Existence / Resistance by Okum January, 2025 Ebo Taylor, Adrian Younge & Ali Shaheed Muhammad are touring the world right now with a new round of what they call "psychedelic afrobeat." The album is titled Ebo Taylor , honoring the 88 year oldGhanaian musician's years as one of highlife music's greatest artsists/ Ebo Taylor JID022 by Ebo Taylor, Adrian Younge, Ali Shaheed Muhammad March, 2025 We've been covering some great Polish music this month, and here's another to hear. Daj Ognia is one a radio listener tipped me off to, a band with roots in both Poland and Scandinavia. This is from their 2023 album, Przedn�wek . Siwy kon, siwy kon, Na siwego siadom, A swojego dam dziadom Gray horse, gray horse, I'll sit on the gray one, And I'll give mine to the grandfathers Przedn�wek by Daj Ognia Released 2023 "Sarah Allen and company should be commended for crafting an instantly recognizable sound that expands the boundaries of instrumental acoustic music." - Lee Blackstone in RootsWorld. Flook just released a single from their upcoming 2025 album, and it is as artful as expected. Here's a taste of Sanju . The Farther Shore/Winter Flower - Single by Flook Single is out January, 2025. Full album in March. The French trio Tako Toki create all their music on instruments made from found objects and scrap they collect and make musicial. It's a clever idea that's been done before, but they take it to a different level, moving from the dead serious, to the slyly imitative, to the downright funny, like this homage to the movie sound track and sound effects artist, Raymond Scott. We have a review coming soon, but dig in and enjoy some now. HIRSUTES FARFELUS - LP by Tako Toki February 2025 Clarinet virtuoso Aur�lie Charneux leads a trio of musicians on Cinqui�me Saison . Joined by Nicolas Puma (double bass) and Simon Leleux (percussion), her compositions explore a 5th season of sounds, improvising to evoke the relationship between humans and nature, the earth and its human adversaries and friends. It can be trance like and soothing, or harsh and demanding. Cinqui�me Saison by Aur�lie Charneux, Simon Leleux, Nicolas Puma This is the second album by Lib�rica , led by bassist Manel Forti� (a favorite around here). It brings together Catalan singers Pere Mart�nez, Valencian Carles D�nia and C�diz-born Antonio Lizana, along with trumpeter and vocalist Alba Careta. It's jazz at its heart, and tradtion in its soul. (Read our review of Manel Forti� & Magli Sare's album 2022 release, re�tornar .) AL� - Iberian Chants by Lib�rica Novalima is a team of DJ-musicians from Lima, Peru who dig deeper into their own roots while staying firmly on the dancefloor. La Danza (Deluxe Version) by NOVALIMA January, 2025 Digital Ngoma is group of musicians from the Indian Ocean island of Mayotte who experiment with traditional beats and electronics. They guarantee "100% made in Mayotte." Digital Ngoma Vol.2 by Kim Canadian string player (mostly mandola and mandolin) Kevin Breit is joined by singer Ariana Gillis on one of the few covers of a Warren Zevon song that has ever been successful and original. I Love You by Kevin Breit Released in 2021 Orchestre Tout Puissant Marcel Duchamp is possibly the best named band in Europe: artful, enigmatic and surprising at every turn. We'll have a review of this soon, but here's a taste of their newest album. While you wait, you can read Martha Willette Lewis' review of their previous album, We're OK. But We're Lost Anyway to get the lowdon on who they are. Ventre unique by Orchestre Tout Puissant Marcel Duchamp January, 2025 We just reviewed Lynn Adib 's 2024 work with Zeid Hamdan, as the duo Bedouin Burger . Here's a taste of some of her solo work, from her 2018 album Youmma . YOUMMA by Lynn Adib Posted January 2025 Wishamalii is an adventurous trio based in Helsinki: singer, oud player and composer Nemat Battah (Palestine/Jordan), pianistand composer Kari Ikonen and Ethiopian-born, Finland-based percussionist Abdissa �Mamba� Assefa (Ethipia). Their newest work, Al-Bahr is rooted in classical Arab music but only as a starting point for new compositions. Ikonen has even refined a piano tuning to play the maqam notes at the heart of this music. Wishamalii - Al-Bahr by Nordic Notes September, 2024 We'll have a review shortly from this album by Polish cymbaly and accordion player Karolina Wegrzyn , but here's a taste of it, a traditional Carpatho-Rusin song that translates as "Whose scythe cuts well." Oy Vesna Krasna by Karolina Wegrzyn January 2025 Two Italians and a Belgian come together in Brussels... sounds like the beginning of a joke, I know. But the sounds that come fromthe instruments, voices and hearts of Flavia Clementi (vocals, shruti box, percussion), Federico Bragetti (cello, vocals, percussion) and Thomas Van Bogaert (guitar, vocals, percussion) is serious, joyous and absobs all the influences a city like Brussels seems to embrace. About RootsWorld : RootsWorld is a world music magazine started in 1993, pretty much at the dawn of the term "world music" as well as the pre-dawn of internet publishing (I suspect this was the first music magazine of any sort published on the www). Our focus is the music of the world: Africa, Asia, Europe, Pacifica and The Americas, the roots of the global musical milieu that has come to be known as world music , be it traditional folk music, jazz, rock or some hybrid.
